title: Use schema-backed Python types for game export JSON instead of raw dicts
description: Python code that loads game exports still mostly returns raw `dict`/`list` values from `json.load()` and then sprinkles ad hoc key lookups and `assert isinstance(...)` checks across callers. The stricter mypy work in PR #1112 made that pain obvious in files like `scripts/analysis/blunder_eval_common.py`, `scripts/export_game.py`, `scripts/analysis/mcp_errors.py`, and `puppeteer/src/puppeteer/leaderboard.py`. We already have versioned game export schemas and migrations under `schemas/`; follow-up should define or generate Python types from that source of truth and make the loaders return typed objects instead of unstructured dictionaries. That would remove repeated manual shape checks, make type errors show up closer to the JSON boundary, and let mypy reason about export fields directly.
